event-e756caa3a053857b.summary: U.S.-led air attacks on Libya intensify as Muammar Gaddafi vows a bloody "long war," with the United States and its European partners facing the prospect of an extended air campaign with uncertain prospects of success.

event-eecb4e79929c285a.summary: The Libyan government announces an immediate ceasefire for all military units effective from 9 pm local time, after allied forces launched a devastating assault on Libya's air defences and declared a no-fly zone effectively in place.

event-7bea950ed17c78dd.summary: President Barack Obama said at a news conference in Chile that while the international military action is aimed only at stopping the killing of Libyan civilians by Col. Muammar el-Qaddafi's forces, "it is U.S. policy that Qaddafi needs to go."

event-30d114fa168ac13e.summary: The U.S. military's campaign in Libya is named Operation Odyssey Dawn, a nickname generated by the Pentagon's computerized NICKA word generator.

event-632473a1a8024e29.summary: Coalition forces bomb Libya for a third straight night, halting advances by Moammar Khadafy's forces.

event-9bbf9b13a566fa03.summary: U.K. Chancellor of the Exchequer George Osborne tells Parliament that the cost of the U.K.'s military operations in Libya will be in the "tens of millions" not "hundreds of millions" of pounds.

event-0082f607dabac13f.summary: Allied air strikes have virtually wiped out Muammar Gaddafi's forces that were attacking the rebel-held town of Misrata, ending five days of bloody assault that cost nearly 100 lives.

event-35c63d95a7aa9c30.summary: Former House speaker Newt Gingrich says there is no consistent standard for military intervention, noting that the Sudanese government has been killing people in Darfur for years while major powers avoided acting, in contrast to the intervention in Libya.

event-ba68512abe16a51b.summary: Libyan rebels recapture the eastern city of Ajdabiya after international air strikes forced government troops to retreat.

event-f1c1ee8d74c919f3.summary: Libyan rebels advance westward to reoccupy Ajdabiya, Brega, Bin Jawad and Ras Lanuf as Libyan army units withdraw under U.S. and allied airstrikes, with analysts saying the next few days may determine whether Gaddafi's forces shatter or hold in a possible protracted stalemate.

event-250626439746064d.summary: The U.S. Secretary of State Hillary Clinton says military strikes on Libya will continue until Muammar Gaddafi complies with the terms of UN resolution 1973, while pro-Gaddafi forces launch a counterattack that drives rebels back from Sirte.

event-6ef3f37d69358727.summary: Muammar Gaddafi's forces launch a powerful counterattack against Libyan rebels, sending them fleeing from towns they had taken two days earlier, while at the London conference William Hague says arming the rebels was not discussed and Hillary Clinton suggests it would be legal.

event-a0b4f2dbef153924.summary: U.S. officials increasingly view a protracted stalemate in Libya as likely, with rebels retaining control of eastern Libya but lacking the capability to drive Moammar Gaddafi from power, as the Libyan government rejects an opposition cease-fire proposal.

event-b64c72be52f25cc1.summary: Libya's opposition calls for a cease-fire if its demands for freedoms are met, as the U.S. says it is withdrawing aircraft used to attack Muammar Qaddafi's forces after adverse weather prevented strikes.

event-e216036df50501c7.summary: The US announces its warplanes will no longer carry out bombing raids in Libya, as the conflict descends into a stalemate and the Pentagon firmly opposes arming and training the rebels.

event-101b420cd7b758ce.summary: The Libyan rebel National Transitional Council promised France 35% of Libya’s crude oil in a secret letter in exchange for total and permanent support.

event-1cba9f7b96b9b0e6.summary: Libyan rebel leaders reject an African Union ceasefire proposal because it does not include the immediate departure of Moammar Gaddafi from power.

event-28ae68930dc8bfdb.summary: Jordan sends fighter aircraft to a European air base to support the no-fly zone over Libya and protect humanitarian flights, according to Foreign Minister Nasser Judeh.

event-54a0c5c46490900f.summary: Libya's deputy foreign minister Abdulati al-Obeidi meets with Greece's foreign minister in Turkey to relay Col. Gaddafi's peace offer to the Europeans, while Italy formally recognizes the Benghazi leadership as the legitimate government of Libya.

event-5c607fb6076cd9a6.summary: Libyan rebel fighters push back into the strategic oil town of Brega, seizing half of it and pledging to drive out Gadhafi's forces, while Italy offers diplomatic recognition to the Libyan opposition council.

event-c2db48676fa6c802.summary: A senior Algerian security official says al Qaeda is exploiting the conflict in Libya to acquire weapons, including surface-to-air missiles, and smuggle them to northern Mali.

event-1c9deaa934e67062.summary: Libya's information minister says Libya is ready to negotiate reforms such as elections or a referendum, but only its own people can decide whether Muammar Gaddafi should stay on as leader, while denying that government forces attacked any civilians.

event-daa07bfebbf18ac9.summary: Libyan rebels reject an African Union peace plan because it did not address their main demand that Muammar Gaddafi quit and proposed reforming a ruling system they want removed.

event-1b4432826781cd46.summary: Libyan rebels call for stronger NATO intervention to stop a government artillery "massacre" in the besieged city of Misrata, where Grad rocket attacks reportedly killed 23 civilians, mostly women and children.

event-e751ce450cfb6daa.summary: NATO foreign ministers meet in Berlin and produce no new military action in Libya, even as forces loyal to Muammar Gaddafi fire rockets onto the rebel-held city of Misrata, killing 23 people.

event-127bd094a928304f.summary: Muammar Gaddafi's government reaches an agreement with the UN to allow humanitarian access to the besieged rebel city of Misrata and other western areas under its control.

event-a3386ad3fb8797ea.summary: The EU has drawn up a "concept of operations" for a military deployment to Libya, dubbed Eufor Libya, but is awaiting UN approval and a request from OCHA before finalizing the mission.

event-dd1d4aa61880c561.summary: Tens of thousands of people are trapped in Misrata and other towns following more than a month of fighting in Libya, which has killed at least 300 and injured upwards of 1,000, including many children.

event-fc25bb614947fd83.summary: The UN humanitarian chief says the Libyan government has promised her access to the besieged rebel city of Misrata, but with no guarantees that the assault by Muammar Gadhafi's forces would cease.

event-22a387fba5342e9d.summary: The U.K. and France announce they are dispatching a joint squad of military advisers to Benghazi to help the Libyan rebel leadership improve its military organizational structures, communications and logistics.

event-854a5bae2f7441bb.summary: The U.N. says the Libyan government's reported use of cluster munitions and heavy weapons in Misrata has caused substantial civilian casualties and may amount to crimes under international law.

event-fd449cc7ef9595a8.summary: The United States, France, and Britain are criticized for mission creep in Libya, with France, Britain, and Italy sending military advisors and the U.S. committing Predator drones and non-lethal aid, moves that risk a stalemate and a prolonged civil war.

event-c6e184709567dc8b.summary: Fighting in Libya's civil war briefly spills over the border into Tunisia as Gaddafi troops battle rebels for control of the Dehiba-Wazin frontier crossing, prompting Tunisia to demand an immediate halt to the violations.

event-a7bbdbf86057f4a9.summary: Libyan rebels and government forces fight for control of the Wazin border crossing into Tunisia, with competing claims of success.

event-99b62dfba9536400.summary: The rebel-held Libyan city of Derna, described as an alleged al-Qa'ida recruitment hub, is profiled amid the uprising against Colonel Gaddafi, with residents rejecting the regime's claims that rebels are drug-fuelled al-Qa'ida agents.

event-58efe867bc2ec36c.summary: A UN official says the Libyan government is forcibly expelling migrants in an attempt to flood Europe with refugees, while UN chief Ban Ki-moon calls for an immediate, verifiable cease-fire in Libya.

event-b50bdd32b172d4fa.summary: Libyan rebels advance on the strategic oil town of Brega and push westward from Misrata while their political leaders visit Washington and London seeking aid, including access to frozen assets, as NATO bombs Tripoli.

event-502338dbd0e61c12.summary: A U.N. envoy holds ceasefire talks in Tripoli, while the International Criminal Court prosecutor prepares to present evidence for possible arrest warrants against Gadhafi for alleged crimes against humanity.

event-0807fe4b97293bd9.summary: The Libyan regime prepares to send a letter to foreign governments proposing an immediate UN- and African Union-monitored ceasefire, unconditional talks with the opposition, amnesty for both sides, and a new constitution, as David Cameron and Barack Obama meet to seek an exit strategy.

event-5041c5b40ae5625c.summary: An African Union summit calls for a halt to NATO airstrikes and a ceasefire in Libya, while the Libyan prime minister says for the first time that his government is ready to talk to rebel leaders to prepare a new constitution.

event-612255cc15406ae4.summary: Spain receives a message from Libyan prime minister Al-Baghdadi al-Mahmoudi seeking a ceasefire with NATO, but the United States says it does not see the offer as credible because it is not accompanied by action.

event-664c279a85cb9ab2.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Stephen Harper vows to ask Parliament to extend Canada's military mission in Libya, saying the extension will not be indefinite and that Canada will not make any modifications to its military contribution to the NATO-led mission.

event-4c05c60dae995f49.summary: NATO and its partners extend the military campaign to protect Libyan civilians for another 90 days.

event-759249e4961ca019.summary: Human Rights Watch accuses Libyan rebels of arbitrarily detaining dozens of civilians suspected of loyalty to Moammar Gadhafi, holding them without trial or due process, with at least one person thought to have died in custody showing signs of torture.

event-4127de1a4fd642be.summary: Canadian Defence Minister Peter MacKay announces that MPs will vote next week on extending Canada's NATO military mission in Libya until the end of September, at an estimated total cost of about $60 million.

event-03657c1fcb138af8.summary: Russia's ambassador to NATO says NATO risks sliding into a ground war in Libya and is trying to kill Muammar Gaddafi.

event-c81220ed2d44d4c6.summary: Congressional opposition is rising to the U.S. role in Libya.

event-2d793b7da6ceaa78.summary: House Speaker John Boehner escalates the constitutional dispute over President Obama's conduct of the war in Libya without congressional approval, criticizing the administration's refusal to provide requested information and mocking its claim that no hostilities are taking place.

event-c6503e9eb6d2ff41.summary: The Libyan government says 19 civilians were killed in a NATO air strike on the home of a top Gaddafi official in Surman, a day after NATO acknowledged killing civilians in a separate strike in Tripoli.

event-3825b3369411c952.summary: Sens. John Kerry and John McCain introduce a Senate resolution expressing support for limited American involvement in the NATO-led military campaign in Libya, while House Speaker John Boehner proposes two competing resolutions, one of which would limit U.S. involvement to a noncombat role.

event-39e81ee439fca575.summary: The House's tea party caucus splits over whether to defund President Barack Obama's military intervention in Libya, with only 31 of 59 caucus members voting for a bill to strip federal dollars for American forces there.

event-3d9ed226053b4b81.summary: Libya's foreign minister travels to Tunisia to discuss a possible settlement to the ongoing conflict, amid arguments that any ceasefire must begin with Gaddafi's departure.

event-87b9c40d86ff4a38.summary: The Transitional National Council welcomed an African Union offer to open talks with the government in Tripoli without the involvement of Muammar Gaddafi, but maintained that his departure was essential for a ceasefire.

event-b82485a8eb559337.summary: The Senate is set to hold a cloture vote on a bill authorizing Obama's Libya military mission for a year, with predictions it will easily clear the 60-vote threshold.

event-db5e46e8caea7d2f.summary: Turkey says it hopes Western and Arab governments working with Libyan rebels can forge the framework of a political solution by next month to help end the Libyan conflict, as Istanbul prepares to host a contact group meeting on July 15.

event-0c525ac9c74c4a12.summary: France denies claims that it is in direct talks with Muammar Gaddafi, while calling for political flexibility over the terms and timing of his departure.

event-d34d652358d0468f.summary: The United States formally recognizes the Transitional National Council as Libya's government, giving the rebel group a diplomatic boost and potential access to billions of dollars in frozen Libyan assets.

event-de4a459d995b8b25.summary: Western and Arab powers begin talks in Istanbul aimed at finding a political solution for Libya that would persuade Muammar Gaddafi to give up power and end the conflict.

event-ba1b36f9c3bc8483.summary: Libyan rebel forces entered the eastern oil town of Brega and fought street battles with forces loyal to Muammar Gaddafi, in the biggest offensive in eastern Libya in weeks.

event-30137576d2814075.summary: Libyan rebel fighters captured a small village south of Sebha, opening a new front within 80 miles of Muammar al-Qaddafi's southern stronghold.

event-4fe17abc2f5d9947.summary: Germany announces a €100m loan to Libya's National Transitional Council, secured against frozen Libyan government funds, to ease a growing humanitarian crisis in rebel-controlled areas.

event-7f23b1326434758d.summary: The U.N. envoy to Libya and the Benghazi-based rebel council discuss ideas for ending the civil war, but no firm peace initiative takes shape, with the rebels rejecting any plan that does not first remove Moammar Gadhafi from power.

event-a0f712fe97ddabbf.summary: France and Britain change their position on Colonel Gaddafi's future, saying he can stay in Libya if he leaves power, shifting toward a negotiated rather than military end to the war.

event-088151d7ea4672d0.summary: Britain expels Moammar Gadhafi's diplomats from London and announces it will hand over Tripoli's embassy and some frozen funds to the rebels in Benghazi.

event-140c3bd98dc933e8.summary: Britain and France accept that Muammar Gaddafi cannot be bombed into exile, as UN envoy Abdul Elah al-Khatib flies to Tripoli for talks and the UK says it would support any agreement reached by the two sides in Libya.

event-8f5b3315fa5baae0.summary: Rebel commander Abdel-Fattah Younis was shot and killed under mysterious circumstances before he could be questioned by opposition authorities over alleged family links to the Qaddafi regime.

event-97a958cbb89af9d3.summary: Barclays Capital reports that Libyan oil production will take years, not months, to return to full capacity once a political solution to the conflict is found.

event-40a181066b3ccf70.summary: Gaddafi's forces are accused of numerous war crimes during the Libyan conflict, including using children as human shields, torturing and executing civilians, and attacking hospitals, as documented in a Physicians for Human Rights report.

event-92febab49c0a5ed4.summary: Rebel fighters in western Libya are regrouping and receiving reinforcements ahead of a planned major offensive toward Tripoli, with a field commander saying they hope to reach the capital before the end of Ramadan.

event-9651d6d6ec013362.summary: Libyan rebel forces claimed victory over Gadhafi forces in the western town of Bir Al-Ghanam after a five-hour battle, with at least eight rebels killed.

event-47b2823d7305bfc8.summary: Rebel forces struggle to defend recent gains in the face of an offensive by troops loyal to Col. Muammar Gaddafi east of Tripoli.

event-b1d6ad3717d61b17.summary: A high-level Tripoli government official, identified as Libya's interior minister or a deputy public security minister, leaves Libya for Egypt amid speculation he may have defected, as rebels report advances toward Tripoli.

event-9b00f21088251c0b.summary: Libyan rebels claimed control of the country's last functioning oil refinery in Zawiya as explosions shook Tripoli and rebel fighters advanced toward the capital.

event-2bde208c3fc01a4c.summary: Rebel forces arrived in Tripoli, where secretly collaborating residents, including doctors and a pharmacist, had prepared to support the rebels.

event-5b1e40a4d7492058.summary: Libyan rebels claim to advance toward Tripoli after capturing the western town of Zlitan from forces commanded by Muammar Qaddafi's son Khamis, though there is no independent confirmation of the reports.

event-962a839a22a9e49d.summary: Libyan rebels advance on Tripoli, supported by a seaborne landing by rebel troops from Misurata and Nato bombing of government positions, as Muammar Gaddafi insists he will not surrender.

event-b5e5cdf42af6680a.summary: The article discusses considerations for helping Libya transition to a stable, independent nation as the Gaddafi regime ends, including challenges of inclusivity, revenge killings, property recovery, and the need for international peacekeepers.

event-f86269fee3e7eb4d.summary: Libyan rebels enter a suburb of Tripoli amid confusion over the situation and Muammar Gaddafi's whereabouts, as the regime's grip appears to be weakening but is not yet over.

event-a5389c83468bdb60.summary: The United Nations announced it is working on a draft resolution to unfreeze Libyan assets and lift sanctions to aid rebels, as foreign countries and oil companies moved to engage with the National Transitional Council amid the endgame of Muammar Gaddafi's regime.

event-f674aed836495791.summary: Hospitals in Tripoli are overwhelmed with wounded as fighting between rebels and Gadhafi forces continues, with rebels battling for control of the airport area and 33 international journalists released after being held for five days.

event-2f1fc12ff350c22e.summary: The Libyan rebels' interim government, the National Transitional Council, announces it is moving from Benghazi to Tripoli as fighting continues around Muammar Qaddafi's last stronghold.

event-87719d1770220449.summary: British and French special forces are on the ground in eastern Libya calling in airstrikes and helping rebel units prepare to assault Sirte, the last coastal town held by pro-Gaddafi forces, according to a rebel officer.

event-15f5635c78eee0b6.summary: The rebel commander in Tripoli announces that disparate rebel fighter groups in the Libyan capital will be brought under a single military command and merged into state institutions after an interim period, forming a new national army.

event-4c7aec500c68111a.summary: International powers meeting in Paris agree to hand over US$15-billion in frozen Gaddafi assets to Libya's National Transitional Council, as the EU rescinds sanctions and the NTC reaffirms a roadmap to democracy with elections planned for 2013.

event-080e34bb92ebdab3.summary: Libyan rebels reject Muammar Gaddafi's offer to negotiate participation in a transitional government, calling it delusional, as sporadic fighting continues near Sirte and the National Transitional Council consolidates control.

event-4e4d898837fe52b5.summary: The Gaddafi regime has ended, with the National Transitional Council preparing to move to Tripoli and rule Libya within the next week or so, though questions remain about the transition.

event-eeded1cc20bb97f9.summary: Libya's National Transitional Council set out an 18-month timetable to elections, while rejecting the deployment of UN military observers.

event-f134f27bef4759b2.summary: The international community moves to avert a humanitarian crisis in Tripoli, where 60 percent of the city lacks water or sanitation and the U.N. is sending five million liters of water and 600 tons of food, as a rebel commander estimates at least 50,000 people have been killed in the six-month war and rebels set a Saturday deadline for loyalists to surrender.

event-0519197de4e91d47.summary: A U.N. team arrives in Libya to re-establish the organization's presence and address water, food and fuel shortages, as the World Food Programme has distributed 600 metric tons of food for 35,500 people for a month.

event-ddfbe60d0daf67aa.summary: Libya’s provisional government says it is closing in on bastions of support for Muammar Gaddafi and plans to resume oil production at key fields within days.

event-486a41151fb1b0f6.summary: Libyan forces launch an assault on Bani Walid, one of the last holdout towns of Muammar Gaddafi's loyalists, and edge towards Gaddafi's birthplace Sirte, though they still meet resistance in Bani Walid.

event-fa14bcb625a23e9e.summary: Libya's interim leader Mustafa Abdel Jalil promises in his first public address from Tripoli to build "a state of institutions, a state of law," while ousted leader Moammar Gadhafi vows in a purported message to "kill until victory."

event-973a4a48ddaa7090.summary: Libya's interim leadership gives residents in Bani Walid a 48-hour notice to leave the city as it sends reinforcements to Bani Walid, Sirte and Sabha, while U.S. assistant secretary of state Jeffrey Feltman arrives in Tripoli on an unannounced visit.

event-a891ea633fe5ad2e.summary: Libyan rebel forces seize control of about 60 percent of Sirte and attack Bani Walid, two of the last strongholds of Muammar Gaddafi.

event-293c30629721b56c.summary: Libyan rebel fighters battle Qaddafi loyalists in Sirte and Bani Walid as the National Transitional Council prepares to form a government, while U.S. President Barack Obama says the American embassy in Tripoli will reopen this week.

event-561e444a7f97c7d1.summary: U.S. ambassador Gene Cretz returns to Libya and raises the American flag over the re-opened U.S. embassy in Tripoli, a month after Muammar Gaddafi was driven from power.

event-2124462b3983c383.summary: Libya's National Transitional Council says it will announce a 22-portfolio "crisis" government within the next few days, while its forces tighten their grip on southern oasis towns but have yet to take the remaining Gaddafi loyalist strongholds of Bani Walid and Sirte.

event-255fa3dcc3e7c4b8.summary: Libyan rebels from the east and west converge on Sirte, the last major loyalist holdout, as rivalry between the two groups reaches new heights ahead of what will likely be the final showdown of the Libyan conflict.

event-2a0c60f63657a310.summary: Members of Libya's National Transitional Council meet for a second day in Benghazi to discuss forming an interim government, with officials saying formation could take up to a week.

event-18f51d21af589f30.summary: Interpol issues a Red Notice calling for the arrest of Saadi Gadhafi, one of Moammar Gadhafi's sons, as Gadhafi loyalists continue stiff resistance in Bani Walid, Sabha and Sirte and $16 billion in Libyan funds are unfrozen.

event-5386f4091fcfb21d.summary: A Turkish Airlines passenger plane landed in Tripoli's Mitiga airport from Istanbul, marking the first international commercial flight to Libya since the ousting of Muammar Gadhafi in August.

event-59ab7752a91fb3a8.summary: Anti-Gaddafi forces prepare a final attack on Sirte, one of the last pro-Gaddafi bastions, as civilians flee and aid agencies warn of a humanitarian crisis.

event-7c1aa9485f8f69e8.summary: Forces loyal to Libya's new government stage a final advance into the last area of Sirte still controlled by pro-Moammar Gadhafi fighters, with an NTC field commander saying his forces control 90% of the city.

event-d35fcc21eee65914.summary: Defence Secretary Liam Fox says the fall of Sirte is "very close" and may bring the Libyan conflict to a close, as NTC forces close in on the last major Gaddafi stronghold.

event-9cd0d443067d6205.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Hillary Clinton visits Tripoli and hails Libya's victory, while pro-Gaddafi fighters continue to hold out in Sirte.

event-65583d87742b34fa.summary: NTC fighters capture Sirte, Muammar Gaddafi's hometown, ending a two-month siege and extinguishing the last significant holdout of troops loyal to the deposed leader.

event-a4e4709f2ebf7cab.summary: Reports say Libya's former leader Muammar Gaddafi was wounded and captured in Sirte, though pro-Gaddafi TV denies the reports as baseless and U.S. officials say they have not received confirmation.

event-cd4bb9707239d7fc.summary: Col Gaddafi is killed, and tribal and religious differences darken Libya's new dawn.

event-cdc17941861a36ce.summary: The article discusses the challenges of building peace and democracy in Libya following the fall of Muammar Gaddafi, emphasizing the need for rule of law, economic recovery, and careful sequencing of elections.

event-fdd3ba90a00b3833.summary: The EU calls on Libya's National Transitional Council to pursue a broad-based reconciliation process and offers assistance with rebuilding the country following the reported death of Muammar Gaddafi.

event-fcd393e9d67e6db8.summary: NATO calls an end to its air war in Libya, while Muammar Gaddafi's family demands the handover of his body for burial after his death in Sirte.

event-1e5c389b3a0e6365.summary: Libya's National Transitional Council plans to declare liberation on Sunday, formally ending the eight-month civil war and beginning a two-year transition to democracy.

event-5c8c4a566ef7e00a.summary: Muammar Gaddafi's corpse is taken off public display in Misrata, but the fallen dictator remains unburied as Libya's National Transitional Council wrangles over his burial.

event-ec9ad1048ef09ec6.summary: Libya’s transitional leader declared the country’s liberation after an 8-month civil war and outlined a post-Gadhafi future with Sharia as the basic source of legislation.

event-60ce05bc06fd6b02.summary: Human Rights Watch demands an inquiry into the apparent execution of at least 53 people at the Mahari Hotel in Sirte, Libya, warning of a trend of killings and abuses by rebel fighters, as Gaddafi is expected to be buried in an unmarked grave.

event-689c226812f5a433.summary: The United Nations Security Council votes unanimously to end NATO's no-fly zone over Libya effective 11:59pm Libyan time on October 31, despite Libya's calls for a delay.

event-960c7bb14aa7623e.summary: NATO voted to end its seven-month Libya mission on October 31, following the UN's decision to end its authorization for the military operation and lift the no-fly zone.

event-4ba78d6e9056d3b1.summary: Libya's outgoing prime minister Mahmoud Jibril calls for speeding up the timetable for elections, warning that an eight-month political vacuum could be dangerous.

event-2d8341192b1f6f76.summary: Libya's ruling National Transitional Council elects academic Abdul Raheem al-Keeb as the new interim prime minister to guide the country toward a new constitution and democratic elections.

event-92c51454194d11e6.summary: Abdul-Raheem al-Qeeb, an academic and former exile, begins selecting his Cabinet after being elected interim prime minister by Libya's National Transitional Council, with two weeks to form a transitional government that is expected to organize elections in the first half of next year.

event-4921012c5d818808.summary: Former officers of Moamer Kadhafi's army meeting in Al-Baida unanimously approve the nomination of Khalifa Haftar as commander in chief of the national army and announce the re-activation of the army, which has yet to be officially reconstituted.

event-3ba503a581b19799.summary: Libya's prime minister-designate Abdurrahim El-Keib said he would name a cabinet of experts on Tuesday to steer the country toward its first fully democratic elections.

event-5f22727786e2ac27.summary: Libya's transitional leaders, including Prime Minister Abdurrahim el-Keib, were sworn in, taking oaths to uphold the revolution's ideals as they prepare to lead the country toward elections.

event-6b34643ad758e970.summary: Canada marked the completion of its Libyan mission with a tribute ceremony on Parliament Hill.

event-b63f888c0a960a12.summary: Senior figures in Libya's new leadership, including NTC chairman Mustafa Abdel Jalil, interim Prime Minister Abdurrahim El-Keib, and Central Bank Governor Saddeq Omar Elkaber, sent a letter to the United Nations appealing for the release of Libyan assets still frozen three months after the civil war ended.

event-9d9e9cfd9ee0c01e.summary: Libya's newly appointed army chief, Major General Khalifa Belgasim Heftir, survives an ambush on his convoy in Tripoli when two gunmen opened fire, though no one in the convoy was harmed and the attackers were arrested.

event-72cdd3dbd0d5fabf.summary: Italy and Libya agree to reactivate their suspended 2008 treaty of friendship, with Italian Prime Minister Mario Monti announcing the decision after meeting Libyan National Transitional Council head Mustafa Abdul-Jalil in Rome.

event-891f5939d6b713a9.summary: Fierce gunbattles between Tripoli and Misrata militias erupt in central Tripoli, leaving at least four fighters dead.

event-e1fcd733a012a1eb.summary: The chairman of Libya's National Transitional Council warns that Libya risks sliding into civil war unless rival militias that filled the vacuum left by Colonel Gaddafi's downfall are brought under control, after a gun battle between militias in Tripoli killed four fighters.

event-646e77fac217d52c.summary: Libya's ruling National Transitional Council says it is ready to form a joint commission with Lebanon to investigate the 1978 disappearance of Shiite imam Mussa Sadr, as a Lebanese delegation led by Foreign Minister Adnan Mansur visits Tripoli.

event-a9e6b029855e750a.summary: Diehard supporters of Muammar Gaddafi seized control of Bani Walid after launching an attack on a former rebel base that killed five people and injured around 30.

event-4bd56c1109c05ec1.summary: A day after townsmen in Bani Walid put to flight a force loyal to Libya's Western-backed interim administration, elders in the former Gaddafi stronghold dismissed accusations they wanted to restore the late dictator's family to power and formed a municipal council after nominal representatives from Tripoli fled.

event-0d836a3000389a3f.summary: A Royal United Services Institute report warns that the Libya campaign’s shift from civilian protection to regime change has made future UN-backed missions to protect civilians less likely, with China and Russia more likely to veto such action, as already seen over Syria.

event-7f24e2e04215b74e.summary: Libya's government showcased a newly painted courtroom in Tripoli to demonstrate its fitness to try Saif al-Islam Gaddafi domestically instead of surrendering him to the International Criminal Court, and asked the ICC to postpone its order to surrender him so it could formally appeal and hold the trial in Tripoli.

event-d9efdb0dee9d048b.summary: ICC Prosecutor Luis Moreno-Ocampo arrives in Tripoli as part of an investigation into charges against Muammar Gaddafi's detained son, Saif al-Islam, whom the ICC has ordered Libya to surrender.

event-37472a4078be1af6.summary: Libya's National Transitional Council passes a law banning political parties based on religion, tribe, or ethnicity ahead of June elections.

event-a482b1990618d187.summary: Delays to Libya's elections spark concern as the NTC steadily loses domestic legitimacy.

event-e959b3da76c5c1c4.summary: Clashes broke out between rival Libyan militias at Tripoli’s international airport after armed gunmen from the al-Awfea Brigade drove armed pickup trucks onto the tarmac and surrounded planes, forcing the airport to cancel flights.

event-a5ccdf33e3b8397f.summary: Hundreds of heavily armed Libyans, some with anti-aircraft weapons, demonstrate in Benghazi calling for Shariah law ahead of scheduled elections.

event-430ee0c5f2a78556.summary: A vehicle carrying Britain's ambassador to Libya, Dominic Asquith, was attacked with rocket-propelled grenades in Benghazi, injuring two bodyguards while the ambassador was unhurt.

event-36407a75241f322d.summary: The International Committee of the Red Cross in Misrata came under attack amid a rapid deterioration in Libya's security situation.

event-9f5bebbefdf3e446.summary: Libya's Election Commission officially delays the national elections from June 19 to July 7.

event-1ece1284dcd0bfb4.summary: Tunisia extradites former Gadhafi prime minister Al Baghdadi Ali al-Mahmoudi to Libya, where he is held in a Tripoli prison to face trial.

event-4b0f379e1c0090bb.summary: Libyans voted in the first parliamentary election since the overthrow and killing of Moammar Gadhafi, amid boycott calls, ballot burnings, and attacks on polling centers in the country's east.

event-6a525f427ed96d06.summary: Jibril's National Forces Alliance wins 39 of the 80 party seats in Libya's first free national elections, while the Muslim Brotherhood's Justice and Construction Party wins 17, with 120 seats going to independents.

event-71c01eb208449dc2.summary: Libya is scheduled to hold its first free election since 1951 for a 200-member General National Congress, though the vote faces uncertainty over security and possible disruption.

event-a37222198506d150.summary: The IMF forecasts Libya's economy will grow 116.6 percent in 2012 after contracting 60 percent in 2011, warning that high public spending is not sustainable over the longer term.

event-7e5b031cbd2e51f9.summary: Final results from Libya's first free nationwide election in half a century placed Mahmoud Jibril's liberal National Forces Alliance ahead with 39 party seats, while the Muslim Brotherhood's Justice and Construction party came second with 17 seats and the balance of power remained with 120 independent candidates.

event-9bd78ab66be3c8b5.summary: Concern is expressed over the Libyan justice system.

event-f27b6c8f71941273.summary: Libya's newly formed national assembly elects former opposition leader Mohammed el-Megarif as the country's interim president.

event-387cf500f61f1659.summary: Libya's ruling National Transitional Council handed over power to a newly elected national assembly in Tripoli, marking the country's first peaceful transition of power in its modern history.

event-69f751018a659ef8.summary: Libya's General National Congress elects Mohamed al-Megaryef, a veteran exiled opponent of Moamer Kadhafi seen as pro-Islamist, as its president in a runoff vote.

event-9cb57fb97b7ef1da.summary: The U.S. Ambassador to Libya, J. Christopher Stevens, and three other Americans were killed in an assault on the U.S. consulate in Benghazi.

event-323855945d8cd7dd.summary: The National Forces Alliance's prime ministerial candidate Mahmoud Jibril is defeated by two votes in favor of Mustafa Abushagur, the outgoing deputy prime minister.

event-6c6aa71b963f60ee.summary: Two American troops were killed in an ambush during a rescue mission for besieged diplomats in Benghazi, Libya, after the U.S. ambassador and another American died in an attack on the consulate.

event-55a44f21ab6a9943.summary: Libyan President Mohammed Magarief says about 50 people have been arrested in connection with the deadly attack on the U.S. consulate in Benghazi, which he said was planned by foreigners linked to al Qaeda.

event-7242935508ae94c0.summary: A large demonstration in Benghazi calls for the disbanding of armed militias, and police, government troops, and activists subsequently sweep militia headquarters following the attack on the U.S. Consulate that killed Ambassador Chris Stevens.

event-16ca317cdab39c81.summary: Protests in Libya condemn Benghazi militias.

event-6aeff4352cc552cd.summary: The Libyan army raids several militia outposts operating outside government control in Tripoli, while the militia suspected in the Sept. 11 attack on the U.S. Consulate says it has disbanded on orders of the country's president.

event-d98178d8f59e8e90.summary: Libyans voluntarily surrendered hundreds of weapons, including six heat-seeking missiles and a tank, in Tripoli and Benghazi as part of a government disarmament drive.

event-40080d6458b819c7.summary: Two suspects in the killing of U.S. ambassador to Libya Christopher Stevens were detained at Istanbul's Ataturk Airport, according to a report by Turkish broadcaster Kanal D.

event-d657f92c3923856a.summary: Libya's parliament ousted newly elected prime minister Mustafa Abushagur in a no-confidence vote after his proposed Cabinet was rejected.

event-6e6391f7fb404196.summary: Ambassador Chris Stevens told officials of security worries on the day he died in the Libya consulate attack, and a special forces chief said he had asked for more, not less, back-up a month before the attack.

event-273f7971dd26755f.summary: Mitt Romney shifts his campaign focus from the economy to criticize the Obama administration's handling of the September 2012 terror attack on the U.S. consulate in Benghazi, Libya, that killed the U.S. ambassador.

event-4610272031d32028.summary: Libya's General National Congress elected Ali Zeidan, a long-time opponent of Moamer Kadhafi, as prime minister and asked him to propose a cabinet within two weeks.

event-1fafac8c848c144a.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Hillary Rodham Clinton says she takes responsibility for the deadly September 11 attack on the U.S. diplomatic mission in Benghazi, Libya, which killed U.S. Ambassador Christopher Stevens and three other Americans.

event-ff0fe4bebc910794.summary: Libya's army is heading towards the former Gaddafi stronghold of Bani Walid hoping to impose order in the town after deadly clashes there, the chief of staff said.

event-01ad9d767ef52ce8.summary: A Canadian commander present at Muammar Gaddafi's capture near Sirte recounts that Gaddafi was beaten by a crowd and then shot twice by a Libyan combatant, despite orders to capture him alive.

event-e14921f6259dca9a.summary: Libyan militias captured Muammar Gaddafi's former spokesman Moussa Ibrahim in the town of Tarhouna, exactly a year after the dictator's death.

event-640364ec8596416e.summary: Protesters and former rebel fighters stormed Libya's national assembly, forcing the cancellation of a vote on Prime Minister Ali Zeidan's proposed coalition government.

event-87b1c1b4f3c3bf7d.summary: Protesters disrupted a session of Libya's National Assembly that was set to vote on a new cabinet headed by Prime Minister-elect Ali Zidan, forcing an early end to the session and leaving Libya without a new government.

event-0b271e8411633c6b.summary: Rival state-sanctioned Libyan militias exchanged gunfire and rocket-propelled grenades in the streets of Tripoli, wounding at least five people, while a car bomb exploded outside a police station in Benghazi, injuring three police officers.

event-4f599dd20ff8e17f.summary: Former Libyan prime minister Al Baghdadi al-Mahmoudi went on trial in Tripoli on charges including corruption and ordering mass rape during the 2011 war, with the hearing postponed to December 10.

event-1cbf31b17a964d94.summary: Libya's first elected government is sworn in under tight security, with Prime Minister Ali Zeidan and his cabinet taking the oath in Tripoli.

event-00e888544d8ffc6e.summary: Libya's independent Authority of National Integrity approved Ali Suleiman Aujali as foreign minister along with two other Cabinet members, though Aujali still requires parliamentary approval before being sworn in.

event-5a74341aa2029e23.summary: President Barack Obama nominates Sen. John Kerry, who had pushed for a no-fly zone over Libya during Moammar Gadhafi's crackdown on rebels and citizens, to be secretary of state.

event-d3233ab92b536d54.summary: Benghazi officials and residents are promoting the city's bid to regain its former status as Libya's business capital, with the $300 million Three Towers project now due for completion in 2015 after delays caused by the uprising against Moammar Gadhafi.

event-8470176beff2925f.summary: On the second anniversary of the February 17 Revolution, Libya faces ongoing tension between revolution and devolution, with federalist and decentralisation forces, especially in Benghazi, continuing to mobilise and organise.

event-2e3e1b55e2943f32.summary: Libya faces political gridlock and security challenges two years after the uprising that ousted Muammar Qadhafi, with the General National Congress stormed by armed protesters and economic progress mixed.

event-34ca0f4cc4dff4ed.summary: Libya is pushing to host the 2017 Africa Cup of Nations, with officials expressing determination to use all resources for the bid, though security concerns remain and a CAF delegation is expected to visit later in the month.

event-19e3ceb958ea1539.summary: Gunmen fired at a convoy of cars carrying Sufian al Qumu, head of the Islamist Ansar al-Sharia militia in the eastern Libyan city of Derna, injuring one person while Qumu escaped with only slight injuries.

event-bfe70af39e45062e.summary: Diplomats warn of growing Islamist violence against western targets in Libya as blowback from the war in Mali, following a car bomb attack on the French embassy in Tripoli.

event-cccad83bfeefbb28.summary: Libyan militiamen surrounded the Justice Ministry in Tripoli, forcing employees out, after three days of storming the Interior Ministry and state-run TV and besieging the Foreign Ministry to demand the removal of Gadhafi-era officials and passage of the isolation law.

event-c7196785ddfff44b.summary: Hundreds of Libyan pro-democracy advocates marched in Tripoli denouncing militias' recent blockade of government buildings and were briefly attacked by supporters of the armed groups.

event-3ac1b3c9787b666c.summary: Libya's parliament votes to ban anyone who held a senior position during Muammar Gaddafi's 42-year rule from government, a move that could unseat the prime minister and other top officials.

event-7e4aa26f17b96336.summary: Armed groups continued their blockade of two ministry buildings in Tripoli, demanding the dismissal of Prime Minister Ali Zeidan, after parliament passed a political isolation law banning Gadhafi-era officials from government.

event-b00db08f167a962e.summary: A former top U.S. diplomat says four members of Army special forces ready to head to Benghazi, Libya, after the deadly assault on the American diplomatic mission were told not to go.

event-239448684696c227.summary: Libyan Prime Minister Ali Zidan promises a Cabinet reshuffle and praises militias as "revolutionaries" after armed groups ended a more than 10-day siege of government institutions.

event-64ab0338b9240ff2.summary: Armed groups surrounding two ministries in Tripoli formed an alliance and expanded their demands to include the resignation of Prime Minister Ali Zeidan, the freezing of a recently released state budget, and the right to form a committee to take charge of the Foreign Ministry.

event-538c8a72c71dabb5.summary: Scores of Libyan militiamen attacked protesters in Tripoli during rallies against the country's unruly militias, beating demonstrators and seizing several young men, while similar protests in Benghazi and Tobruk passed without violence.

event-10dc503a34f768f0.summary: Libya's national assembly approves Mohammed Khalifa al-Sheikh as the new interior minister after incumbent Ashour Shuail submitted his resignation.

event-94db4496793a5c74.summary: Libyan parliament chief Mohammed al-Megarif resigns after lawmakers passed a law banning former regime officials from senior government posts.

event-47e4c9f607551553.summary: Libya's General National Congress, under pressure from armed militias, passed a controversial Political Isolation Law barring former Gaddafi regime officials from senior government posts for a decade, prompting parliamentary chief Mohammed al-Megarif to resign.

event-18fff67fe70dba15.summary: Clashes between the Libya Shield brigade and protesters in Benghazi left 31 dead and at least 120 wounded, prompting the United Nations mission to Libya to call for maximum restraint.

event-50c2de334b02606d.summary: Libya's army will take control of a militia's bases in Benghazi after clashes in which 31 people were killed.

event-2c28e097354c1527.summary: A judge, Mohammed Houidi, was shot dead by gunmen outside a court in the eastern Libyan city of Derna.

event-d152cc7e51fa29b7.summary: Libya's prosecutor's office says Seif al-Islam Gadhafi, former spy chief Abdullah al-Senussi, and other former regime officials will stand trial in the first half of August for crimes committed during the 2011 uprising.

event-3650c0835e73bc5c.summary: Libya's prime minister told ethnic Africans displaced from Tawergha during the 2011 civil war to delay their planned return, while Human Rights Watch urged Libyan judicial authorities to drop criminal charges against two politicians facing the death penalty.

event-73227527a9c5d6f8.summary: Libya's largest political party, the National Forces Alliance, announces it will boycott sessions of the General National Congress starting Thursday, protesting delays in drafting a constitution.

event-f1565d4b76e46dc7.summary: The Libyan government regained control of its interior ministry building in Tripoli from an armed group that had besieged it for a week.

event-ef8fc132abda1394.summary: A Libyan air force colonel, Fathi al-Omami, was shot dead in the eastern city of Derna by assailants in a car as he visited a shop he owned.

event-b2ef9b06122c17ac.summary: Three Libyan ethnic minorities—the Amazigh, Tibu, and Tuareg—announced they would boycott an election of a committee to draft a new constitution, saying the constitutional committee would not be fully representative.

event-20e1ea609631edb3.summary: The International Criminal Court rejected Libya's request to suspend the handover of Seif al-Islam Kadhafi, ruling that Tripoli remains obliged to surrender him to the ICC.

On 2011-10-23 Libya's transitional leader declared the country's liberation after an 8-month civil war and outlined a post-Gadhafi future with Sharia as the basic source of legislation.

Diehard supporters of Muammar Gaddafi seized control of Bani Walid after launching an attack on a former rebel base that killed five people and injured around 30.

Libya's information minister says Libya is ready to negotiate reforms such as elections or a referendum, but only its own people can decide whether Muammar Gaddafi should stay on as leader, while denying that government forces attacked any civilians.
